data.body_html:
Planning a stag weekend in Marbella for 2028? A yacht charter is the ultimate way to celebrate, combining sun, sea, and style. But how much does it actually cost? This budget breakdown covers everything from entry-level boats to luxury yachts, hidden extras, and insider tips to keep your group on track. Whether you're a party of 8 or 12, our fleet departs from Puerto Banús – the heart of Marbella's glamorous marina.

Why a Yacht Charter Works for a Stag Weekend

Marbella offers over 300 days of sunshine a year, calm Mediterranean waters, and a coastline dotted with exclusive coves like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés. A private yacht gives your group total freedom: swim, sunbathe, blast music, or explore the coast from Puerto Banús to Estepona. No queues, no crowds – just you and the lads. With a licensed skipper handling navigation, you can focus on the celebration.

2028 Pricing: Entry-Level Yachts (Up to 11 Guests)

For smaller groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are the most budget-friendly options. Prices start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full 8-hour day. Both include a skipper, fuel, drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava), light snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT. That works out to around €104 per person for a half-day trip – excellent value for a stag do.

2028 Pricing: Luxury Yachts (Up to 12 Guests)

If your group wants to go big, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is a showstopper. It costs €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter and includes a free jet ski – perfect for adrenaline seekers. For larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) or Canados 86 (26m, 12 pax), pricing is available on request via WhatsApp. These boats offer flybridges, sun pads, and spacious saloons for the ultimate luxury experience.

What's Included – And What's Not

Every charter in our fleet includes: a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). There are no hidden fees. However, you may want to budget extra for:

  • Premium catering – upgrade to a BBQ or tapas platter (approx. €25–€50 per person)
  • Watersports – jet ski, paddleboard, or snorkel gear (from €100 per item)
  • Gratuities – 10–15% of the charter cost is customary for the skipper
  • Transport – taxis or transfers from your accommodation to Puerto Banús (€20–€40 per group)

Total extras typically run €200–€500 depending on your choices.

How to Split Costs Per Person

For a group of 10 on an Azimut 39 at €2,299 for 8 hours, the per-person cost is just €230. Add €50 for food and drinks upgrades, and you're looking at €280 per person for a full day on the water. Compare that to a night out in Marbella (€100–€150 per person for dinner and drinks), and the yacht offers better value for a unique experience. For the Mangusta 80 with 12 people, the 4-hour charter works out to €393 per person – still competitive for a luxury yacht with a jet ski.

Tips to Save Money on Your Stag Weekend Yacht

Book early – peak season (June–August 2028) sees high demand, so reserve at least 3 months ahead. Choose a half-day charter (4 hours) instead of a full day to keep costs down while still enjoying swimming and sightseeing. Bring your own food and extra drinks to avoid catering upgrades. Finally, consider a weekday charter (Monday–Thursday) for better availability and potential discounts.

Best Boats for a Stag Weekend

Our fleet has something for every vibe. For a party atmosphere, the Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) offers speed and style. For a relaxed day with space to lounge, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) is ideal. If you want to impress, the Mangusta 80 (white or grey) is a head-turner. For a smaller, budget-friendly option, the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) is perfect for a tight-knit group. View the full fleet on our Marbella yacht charter page.

Sample Itinerary for a Stag Weekend

Depart Puerto Banús at 11:00, cruise past the Golden Mile and La Concha mountain. Stop at Cala del Faro for swimming and photos (30 min). Head to Cala Cortés for lunch and jet ski fun (1.5 hours). Then cruise to Cabopino for a final swim before returning to Puerto Banús by 16:00. This 5-hour itinerary fits perfectly into a half-day charter and leaves the evening free for Marbella's nightlife.
